result.title: The Token-Energy Law of LLM Decode: Active Bytes and Realized Time Account for Joules per Token
result.summary: Energy-efficient deployment of large language models requires understanding how model architecture, hardware, and serving settings shape energy per generated token. We introduce the Token-Energy Law, a compact, interpretable model of GPU-board energy per output token for dense, full-history decoding. It relates token energy to two core dimensions: active bytes and realized decode time. Active bytes describe logical byte demand per output, separating dense weights shared within a decode iteration from private key--value (KV) histories read and updated for each request. Realized decode time is the elapsed decode duration divided by the number of output tokens produced. We combine the two byte coordinates and time in a common affine form, with coefficients calibrated for each model and hardware/runtime configuration. This formulation explains how batching amortizes shared-weight work, longer attended histories increase private KV demand, and throughput determines the time-associated cost per output. Our experiments cover three models under BF16 decoding on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, including two-GPU tensor parallelism on Hopper. Using fixed coefficients and observed decode time, held-out condition-mean energy estimates differ from measurements by at most 3.73%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「Token-Energy Law」：用 active bytes（区分共享权重与逐请求 KV 历史读写）和 realized decode time 两个维度，以仿射形式建模每个输出 token 的 GPU 板级能耗，并在三种模型、Hopper/Blackwell 及双卡张量并行下验证，留出条件均值误差不超过 3.73%。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文把能耗拆成权重摊销、KV 历史读取与吞吐相关时间成本，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 等额外推理步的实际成本核算提供可核查的量化视角，本身不涉及视觉推理或 latent 状态。
